kinds: The firmware UI renders a complete screen from the test’s control inputs or explicit host settings.

The firmware’s boot display function writes to a simulated LCD.
The firmware’s update display function runs with the delay suppressed.
The firmware draws its clip grid, header and footer from test memory.
The firmware draws its clip key page and header from test memory.
A simulated keyboard edit is saved and reloaded through the firmware project code.
The test runs calibration display code with supplied control values.
The firmware handles simulated keyboard inputs and renders the resulting step lane.
The firmware draws its pad calibration screen from test memory.
A test calls the firmware’s preview painter directly.
The production recovery or calibration code runs against simulated board inputs and a RAM display.
The firmware renders the oscillator with the selected control lock in simulated memory.
The firmware’s normal startup loop runs with simulated flash, controls and a RAM display.
The firmware guard runs with the Elite or Pro register inputs recorded from target emulation.
